claim_assessments.scope: Incompatibility of the exact fixed complex dataset, with all five numerical inequalities, the fixed flag, off-axis jet system, and independent blowup witness; no additional nefness or pseudo-effectivity.
claim_assessments.justification: All seven geometric implications supply a nonzero determinant whose order at the same independent diagonal point is simultaneously greater and less than 3R/4 for arbitrarily large good primes.

Finite descent and separate smoothness, projectivity, ampleness, birationality and jet opens are available. A generated twist bounds negative quotient ranks and degrees, leaving finitely many projective Quot schemes with empty geometric generic fibres. Noether normalization applies after the good-model localization and supplies closed points in every characteristic outside a finite set. The fixed complete-intersection witness tests all effective divisors on each reduction.

Products give a triangular jet basis without factorials; the finitely fixed fillers are local units. The top Frobenius monomial degree is covered by the stated threshold. The constant-coordinate projection from the free module A_*[z]/(z^p-z_0^p) selects precisely p-divisible weights without discarding nilpotents, giving full rank p^(2n) at the jet base pair and generically.

Etale-local parameter differences identify the global truncated symmetric associated graded. Complementary multiplication is a perfect GL-equivariant pairing with top character (det V)^(p-1). Summing complementary Chern classes gives c_1(E_p)/s=B_p/p+(p-1)K_W/(2p), as a rational divisor identity valid also in characteristic 2.

Langer applies with a nef line of uniformly bounded degree and generated tangent twist. Serre-duality generation of rounded Frobenius twists bounds every tensor quotient by i L_min(V); socle duality then bounds all truncated maximal slopes by (p-1)K_W.C+nc. No tensor semistability or interchange of characteristic and Frobenius-iteration limits is assumed.

Restriction filtrations stop after negative ample twists, with no uniform stopping index needed. Curve evaluation and finite tuple counts bound each graded piece by e_j P(p); summing ranks gives sP(p), not an additional factor for the number of pieces. The leading coefficient is 7^n H^n and nonnegative lower coefficients give rank_diagonal/R <= A+E/p.

Every full-rank selection of weight-labelled source columns gives actual external-product determinant factors with averaged slot weights in [0,q]. The inverse source determinant has the required positive weight sign. The error numerator belongs to the fixed k_0-element divisor list, and strict transforms give a uniform order bound for all factor sections, including those that exist only on a reduction.

Order-adapted bases have independent leading forms in each degree; their external products remain independent in the two-parameter-set bigrading. This gives the upper order for the chosen determinant. Constant residue-field row operations at the same independent diagonal point give determinant membership in m^(R-t), proving the lower order for that identical section.

supported_scope: Ordinary mathematical reconstruction of the exact original thm:finite-data and its seven proof obligations.
Good reductions of unbounded characteristic preserving minimum cotangent slope through finitely many proper Quot loci, without strong semistability.

Generic full rank, global truncated filtration, uniform slope and flag bounds, column-independent normalized determinant classes, and contradictory orders of the same determinant at the independently fixed point.
The displayed C_0,C_gamma,E,P_* refinement is substantiated as a numerical threshold for good reductions, conditional on the stated dataset and correctly applied primary propositions.

external_assumptions.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 32.10.1, parts (1)-(3), stable tag 01ZM.
external_assumptions.actual_hypotheses: A directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, and its limit.
external_assumptions.source_conclusion: Finitely presented schemes descend; morphisms between finite-presentation models descend later; equal base-changed morphisms become equal at a later index.
external_assumptions.application: The finite list over the complex numbers descends along spectra of finitely generated integer subalgebras. Smoothness and ampleness are separately retained, not attributed to this lemma.
external_assumptions.reading_status: Local excerpt and actual public primary statement parts (1)-(3) read; hypotheses and application match.

external_assumptions.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 37.27.5, stable tag 0559.
external_assumptions.actual_hypotheses: Finite-type morphism to an irreducible base with geometrically irreducible generic fibre.
external_assumptions.source_conclusion: All fibres are geometrically irreducible after restriction to a nonempty open subscheme of the base.
external_assumptions.application: The integral good-model base and generic fibres satisfy these hypotheses. Smoothness separately provides geometric reducedness and hence geometric integrality.
external_assumptions.reading_status: Local excerpt and actual public primary statement read; hypotheses and application match.

external_assumptions.citation: Nitin Nitsure, Construction of Hilbert and Quot Schemes, 29 April 2005, Theorem 5.1 (Grothendieck), Section 5, printed page 24.
external_assumptions.actual_hypotheses: Noetherian base, projective morphism, relatively very ample line bundle, coherent source sheaf, and fixed rational Hilbert polynomial; the Quot functor parametrizes coherent quotients flat over the parameter scheme with proper support.
external_assumptions.source_conclusion: The fixed-Hilbert-polynomial Quot functor is represented by a projective scheme over the base.
external_assumptions.application: A generated twist bounds negative quotient ranks and degrees, leaving finitely many Hilbert polynomials. Their proper images are closed and miss the geometric generic point by the given minimum-slope condition.
external_assumptions.reading_status: Primary local PDF page 24, full-text theorem, Quot definition on printed pages 3-4, and explanation of Theorem 5.1 on printed pages 27-28 read.

external_assumptions.citation: Adrian Langer, Semistable sheaves in positive characteristic, Annals of Mathematics 159 (2004), 251-276, Corollary 2.5, printed page 258; Section 2 setup pages 256-257.
external_assumptions.actual_hypotheses: Smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, fixed nef slope polarizations, torsion-free sheaf of rank rho, and a nef divisor A such that T_X(A) is globally generated. Semistability of the sheaf is not required.
external_assumptions.application: On the curve the product of polarizations is empty. A degree at most max(4g-2,0) choice is justified by tangent degree and Serre duality; rank n and the retained minimum slope give L_min(V)>=-c/(p-1). The tensor-quotient estimate is proved separately, not quoted as tensor semistability.
external_assumptions.reading_status: Primary local PDF pages 256-258, matching full-text setup and Corollary 2.5, and both historical attribution files read.

effective_threshold.conclusion: For each good prime p>=P_*, a nonzero determinant of size R=p^(2n) would satisfy ord(sigma)/R >= 1-rank_diagonal/R > 3/4 and ord(sigma)/R <= 80 epsilon+2 C_gamma/p < 3/4. Good primes are unbounded.
effective_threshold.precise_limitation: P_* is not a computed bound on all bad primes. Exact inequalities with arbitrary real epsilon are an ordinary mathematical conclusion, not a directly replayed rational-scalar Lean theorem.
